session_1.text: Hey, I'm thinking about adding a Math minor. Do you know what the requirements are?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Hi Alice! I can help you with that. Are you looking for the standard Math minor course sequence?
Yes, just the regular Math minor. I want to make sure I don't miss any required classes.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Absolutely. The Math minor usually includes a sequence of foundational mathematics courses.
Could you list the specific courses I need to complete for the minor?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Of course! The Math minor requires you to complete five specific math courses.
Which five are those?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: You'll need to take MATH 150, MATH 151, MATH 152, MATH 250, and MATH 251 for the Math minor.
Thanks! So no electives or additional requirements beyond those five courses?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Correct, just those five core math courses are required for the Math minor.
That's good to know. I guess that's easier to track than I thought!
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Yes, as long as you complete those five, you should be all set for the minor.
Would you recommend spreading these courses out over two or three years?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Many students do spread them over two or three years, depending on their primary major and course load.
If I take MATH 150 and 151 early, then 152 afterward, is that okay?
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: That's a solid plan! Then you could complete MATH 250 and 251 after the first sequence.
Awesome. I’ll put those courses down in my planner.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Let me know if you’d like help mapping out a timeline for completing these courses.
Thanks! I might check in as I go through my course selection.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Happy to help, Alice! Good luck planning your Math minor.
Appreciate it! I’ll reach out again if I have questions on the requirements later.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: Sure thing, Alice. Just let me know anytime you need clarification!
Will do! Have a good day.
session_1.speaker: Alice

session_1.text: You too, Alice! Take care.

session_2.text: I’m ready to start checking my courses for the Math minor. Where do I find my most up-to-date course list?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Do you have a file or document where you keep track of your courses and grades, Alice?
I remember saving it somewhere, but I can’t recall the exact name.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: It might be named something with your name or 'Course_List'. Let's check for that.
Yes, I think that rings a bell. Could it be in my data folder?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: If you have a folder like '/testbed/data', there might be an Excel file in there with your course details.
I found a file named 'Thomas_Robinson_Course_List.xlsx'. Does that have all my information?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Yes! The course information for Thomas Robinson is in 'Thomas_Robinson_Course_List.xlsx'.
Perfect. Does it also list my grades along with the courses?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Absolutely. That file should include your courses, grades, terms, and years.
Awesome, I'll open that up now.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: If you need help interpreting anything in the file or cross-checking the Math minor requirements, just ask.
Thanks! Looking at the sheet now.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Let me know if any course code or grade is unclear.
It’s organized by term and year too—makes it easier to track my progress.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: That’s handy, especially for seeing how the courses fit with your minor plan.
If I wanted to check my progress for another minor later, is this the right file to use?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Yes, 'Thomas_Robinson_Course_List.xlsx' should have all the up-to-date course information you’ll need for any requirement check.
Great. Is this also where I track physics or general education requirements?
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Yes, all your courses—math, physics, and others—should be in that Excel file.
Very convenient. I’ll make sure to keep it updated.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Smart move! Consistent updates will make reviewing your requirements much easier.
Thanks for confirming! I might need your help cross-checking the requirements soon.
session_2.speaker: Alice

session_2.text: Of course, just let me know when you’re ready to review!

session_3.text: Now that I've compared my course list to the Math minor requirements, where should I record my answer?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: For these types of checks, it’s best to submit your answer in a designated file.
Is there a specific file name I need to use?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: Yes, please put your answer in a file named 'answer.txt'.
Should I include any explanation or just the final answer?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: You only need to write your answer—either 'Yes' or 'No'—in the 'answer.txt' file. No explanation is required.
Just 'Yes' or 'No'—nothing else?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: Exactly, a single word: either 'Yes' or 'No' on its own line.
What if I put a comment after the answer just for myself?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: For official submission, the answer.txt file should only contain 'Yes' or 'No', with nothing else.
That’s clear! That’ll definitely keep the checking process simple.
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: It also helps ensure your answer is easy to find and evaluate later.
So, I’ll just write either 'Yes' or 'No' into 'answer.txt' and save it in the same directory?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: Yes, save 'answer.txt' in the same directory as your other files, like your course list.
Great, thanks! Is this the same process for other requirement checks?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: Yes, whether it’s for the Math minor or some other program, just record your result in 'answer.txt'.
Very efficient! No need for formatting or anything fancy?
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: No formatting needed, just one word: 'Yes' or 'No'.
Understood. I’ll do that now.
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: Perfect! Let me know if you need help with anything else.
Thank you, I appreciate your help!
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_3.text: You’re welcome, Alice! Good luck finishing up your requirement review.
Thanks! If I get stuck, I’ll reach out again.
session_3.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Good morning! How are you today?
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Good morning, Alice! I'm doing well—thanks for asking. How about you?
I'm good! Got a busy day planned, lots of meetings.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Sounds like a packed schedule. Do you have time for a break in between?
I hope so! I might sneak out for a coffee later.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: A coffee break always helps. Do you take it with cream and sugar?
Just milk, usually. How about you?
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: If I could drink coffee, I'd go for a classic black. It's simple and strong!
Haha, fair! If you could try a pastry, which one would you pick?
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: I'd probably try a croissant—light, flaky, and classic.
Nice choice. I might try to grab one if the bakery isn’t too busy.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Go for it! Fresh pastries in the morning are the best.
Do you have any tips for keeping energy up during long meetings?
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Try keeping water nearby, and stand up to stretch if you can. It helps keep you alert.
That's actually really helpful advice. I'll try that today.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Glad to help! Let me know if you want any more productivity tips.
Sure! What about managing my inbox, it’s overflowing again.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Set aside a set time each day to process emails. Sorting by urgency can work wonders!
That makes sense. I might block off some time after lunch.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Perfect timing—your focus will be sharper after a meal.
Thanks! I should get ready for my first call now.
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: Good luck with the call! Ping me if you need anything later.
Will do. Have a great morning!
session_4.speaker: Alice

session_4.text: You too, Alice! Enjoy your day.

session_5.text: Hey! Do you have any tips for getting into a productive morning routine?
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Hi Alice! Starting with a consistent wake time and some light exercise can really boost your mornings.
I've been trying to wake up at the same time, but it’s hard when I stay up late reading.
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Going to bed at the same time each night can help. Maybe try a wind-down routine before sleep?
That's a good idea. I could read for a set amount of time and then put my book away.
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Exactly! Setting an alarm as a reminder to start winding down can work, too.
Thanks! What's your favorite time of the day?
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: I don’t have a body clock, but I enjoy mornings because it’s when many people are full of energy.
Makes sense! I do feel more focused after breakfast.
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: A good breakfast is the best way to fuel your day. Do you have a go-to breakfast meal?
Usually toast or some oatmeal. What about you—if you could eat?
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: I think I’d try pancakes—not just for the taste but because they seem fun to make.
Pancakes are great—especially with berries. Now I’m getting hungry!
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Maybe treat yourself to a nice breakfast tomorrow!
That might be my plan. Do you recommend working out in the morning or at night?
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: It depends on your schedule, but mornings can boost your mood and energy for the whole day.
I’ll give morning workouts a try. Maybe just a short stretch at first.
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: That’s a great start! Gentle stretching gets your body ready for anything.
Thanks for all the advice. I’m going to write out a routine tonight.
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Great idea. Checking off each step can make your routine more rewarding.
I love ticking things off lists!
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: It gives a nice sense of accomplishment, doesn’t it?
It really does. Thanks again for the encouragement!
session_5.speaker: Alice

session_5.text: Anytime, Alice! Have a fantastic day ahead.
